record.title: Laos and Thailand close four Nakhon Phanom local crossing points
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Thakhek–Nakhon Phanom municipal ferry; Pak Nam Xe Bang Fai (Nong Bok)–That Phanom; Pak Nam (Hinboun)–Tha Uthen; Pak Beng–Ban Nat Tha local crossing.
record.crossings: Thakhek port; Pak Nam Xe Bang Fai; Pak Nam Hinboun; Pak Beng (opposite Ban Nat Tha).
record.direction: Local crossing access; travellers redirected to bridge
record.exceptions: Third Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge remained an alternative.
record.imposing_authority: Lao authorities and Thailand’s Nakhon Phanom administration
record.relationship: Earlier local/river phase than EA016 national March 30 restrictions; not four separate event rows.
record.status_observation: Thakhek–Nakhon Phanom ferry observed operating October 3 2022; endpoints for three other local posts unresolved.
record.uncertainty: Four crossing names recovered in Thai governor-notice reporting; romanizations vary. October 3 2022 endpoint applies only to the Thakhek–Nakhon Phanom ferry. No assumption that all four reopened together or with national May 2022 easing.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. No operational duration calculated.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Thai notice reporting and reporter observation establish stopped river passage.
March 17, 2020 at 14:00 is announced; reporter saw the final Thai ferry about 15:00.
October 3, 2022 ferry restoration is supported by substantial indexed official/local passages after both direct accesses failed.

Four local posts named in Thai notice; endpoint only Thakhek–Nakhon Phanom ferry, not all four.
No single multi-post interval; national reopening dates cannot substitute for ferry restoration.
